method: Architecture-focused source inspection of 17 public repositories, selected for direct scrolling relevance, Mac adoption, platform techniques and lineage. Popularity was checked with live GitHub star counts; small emerging projects are included for technical relevance. This is not an exhaustive census or full audit of every file. This architecture-study phase did not build, install or benchmark upstream projects; subsequent engine evaluation is recorded separately.

target.basis: Public product and setup pages; no public ChainYourMac implementation was identified in the repository search.

recommendation: For the requested Rust direction, use a Rust background engine with a SwiftUI/AppKit shell. Evaluate Paneru as the closest existing engine candidate and Rift as the second candidate. For a fresh Mac-only build, Swift throughout likely reduces development effort; there is no measured Rust-versus-Swift winner in this study.

repositories.description: A sliding, tiling window manager for MacOS.
repositories.finding: The closest existing Rust foundation: persistent horizontal strips, stacks, tabbed display, raw gestures, inertia, session restore and native Spaces. Layout state and OS frame commits are separate systems; IPC currently uses typed Mach messages.
repositories.caveat: The current frame commit systems use parallel worker iteration. The architecture document's blanket main-thread AX rule is stale. Parallel writes can still hold a frame schedule open; responsiveness needs measurement before adopting the engine. Edge parking and adjacent displays need physical testing.

repositories.description: Free, open-source tiling window manager for Apple Silicon Macs, with Niri-style scrolling containers and Hyprland-style Dwindle BSP.
repositories.finding: A substantial native scrolling implementation, also offering a BSP layout. Its per-application AX workers accept batched frame requests; mailboxes replace pending work by window ID and generation checks cancel stale writes. Viewport motion separates gesture, spring and deceleration states.
repositories.caveat: Its broad feature set adds integration surface. Use as a reference for Mac behavior and asynchronous frame delivery. Evaluate the GPL distribution model before choosing it as the product's code foundation.

repositories.description: Nehir — a tiling window manager for macOS
repositories.finding: A scrolling-focused fork of OmniWM. Reveal policy distinguishes explicit navigation from automatic focus recovery, with columns, viewport state and per-application frame application. Especially useful for studying focus behavior after window closes and stack changes.
repositories.caveat: Shares a code lineage with OmniWM, so these are not independent implementations. Its README documents parked windows surviving a crash and neighboring-display bleed. Those are product requirements to solve, not language problems.

repositories.description: Tiled scrollable window manager for MacOS
repositories.finding: A compact, readable model of Mac scrolling tiling. Arrays of columns, an anchor window and virtual x positions drive layout. The gesture module tracks touch identities and computes movement from normalized touch positions.
repositories.caveat: A useful fast prototype route for personal use. A standalone consumer app would still need packaging and its own native settings experience. The project explicitly documents off-screen margins and vertically arranged monitors as workarounds.

repositories.description: A fast, native scrollable-tiling window manager for macOS, inspired by Niri.
repositories.finding: An emerging scrolling manager with a useful separation between pure layout, runtime intent and Mac frame delivery. Its AX coordinator rejects stale generations, rebases animation onto completed positions and keeps display callbacks separate from AX writes.
repositories.caveat: Small adoption compared with the established projects. Its performance document includes historical measurements and later revalidation that did not establish a general gain. Trackpad navigation is outside its documented V1 scope. Treat its targets as targets, not benchmark guarantees.

repositories.description: a tiling window manager for macos
repositories.finding: A Glide-derived manager that now includes scrolling columns as well as other layouts. Its scrolling implementation keeps persistent column IDs and a camera offset. Its display-link bridge publishes one replaceable tick rather than queuing stale display events.
repositories.caveat: A particularly relevant second Rust candidate, with a broader scope than a strip-only product. It intentionally uses undocumented APIs. GitHub's license classifier returns NOASSERTION; the checked-in LICENSE contains Apache 2.0 and origin attribution.

repositories.description: A tiling window manager for macOS
repositories.finding: Strong separation between system wrappers, pure model and side-effecting actors. Per-application threads handle AX work; transaction IDs keep delayed feedback from undoing newer intent. Animation requests can replace an active animation.
repositories.caveat: Its main layout model is a tiling tree, so adopting it would require scrolling behavior. Its actor design is more relevant here than copying its complete layout engine. Package metadata explicitly offers a dual license.

repositories.finding: The strongest behavioral reference for scrolling columns, viewport fitting, gestures and display reconnect policy. Its ScrollingSpace owns columns separately from view offset; layout tests include generated sequences of operations.
repositories.caveat: Niri is a compositor that controls rendering. Its Smithay, Wayland and rendering dependencies do not provide a Mac window-control backend. Reimplementing its behavior on macOS is a different task from compiling it for Mac.

repositories.description: Tiled scrollable window management for GNOME Shell
repositories.finding: The original workflow reference uses columns of MetaWindows and a clipped container of window clones. Scrolling moves that container; real window positions are committed after animation. Gesture handling integrates with GNOME Shell.
repositories.caveat: That animation strategy depends on compositor-level GNOME access. The fact that JavaScript drives it is another reason not to infer smoothness from implementation language alone.

repositories.description: AeroSpace is an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS
repositories.finding: Recursive tree layouts, configurable rules and emulated workspaces. MacApp creates a dedicated AX thread for each application. MacWindow parks hidden-workspace windows in corners; layout code accounts for monitor-boundary quirks.
repositories.caveat: A mature source of platform techniques rather than a ready-made scrolling layout. Its own workspace system differs from keeping an independent strip in each native macOS Space.

repositories.description: A tiling window manager for macOS based on binary space partitioning
repositories.finding: A valuable platform reference. Frame application uses size, position, then size again to work around macOS constraints. The animation path uses window proxies, SkyLight transactions and a display link. Source comments explicitly discuss delayed AX events and stale caches.
repositories.caveat: Its BSP model differs from scrolling. Basic operation and its optional scripting addition have different requirements: the README marks partial SIP disabling as optional for elevated features. Do not generalize that all yabai use requires disabling SIP.

repositories.description: Automatic tiling window manager for macOS à la xmonad.
repositories.finding: An example of layout calculation returning frame assignments that execute through cancellable operations. ScreenManager tracks per-Space layouts and cancels outdated reflow operations. Useful for native Space lifecycle and app exceptions.
repositories.caveat: Its layouts are screen reflows rather than a persistent scrolling camera. Much of the application-level machinery would be unnecessary in a narrowly scoped strip implementation.

repositories.description: Move and resize windows on macOS with keyboard shortcuts and snap areas
repositories.finding: A strong reference for reliable frame placement and stubborn windows. StandardWindowMover chooses whether to resize or move first based on screen geometry; BestEffortWindowMover corrects the accepted frame when the requested size cannot be achieved.
repositories.caveat: A snapping utility, not an automatic scrolling layout engine. Its platform edge cases and settings experience are more transferable than its action model. The checked-in license is MIT despite GitHub's classifier returning NOASSERTION.

repositories.finding: A useful native interaction reference. WindowEngine resolves window state, handles fullscreen and may invoke supported system window actions. Its resize animation caches the last frame and cancels a previous animation for the same window.
repositories.caveat: A snapping-oriented interaction model. Its per-window resize animation does not by itself solve synchronized movement across a strip of different applications.

repositories.description: Staggeringly powerful macOS desktop automation with Lua
repositories.finding: The native foundation under PaperWM.spoon. Its window extension bridges Lua to native window objects; its instant frame setter documents the size-position-size sequence and Enhanced UI handling. UI-element watchers expose native notifications.
repositories.caveat: Excellent for experimentation and investigating platform behavior. Shipping a focused app on it means inheriting an entire automation host and its lifecycle.

repositories.description: A lightweight macOS window and app manager scriptable with JavaScript
repositories.finding: A small scriptable Mac window-management foundation. AXObserver bridges app notifications; PHWindow sets a frame with the same size-position-size sequence and verifies the result. Useful for a minimal native API surface.
repositories.caveat: Scripting primitives rather than a complete scrolling product. The license explicitly excludes the app icon assets from MIT coverage.

repositories.description: Spectacle allows you to organize your windows without using a mouse.
repositories.finding: A historical snapping reference and predecessor acknowledged by Rectangle. StandardWindowMover reads the current rectangle and composes frame-setting with another mover, illustrating a small platform abstraction.
repositories.caveat: Archived and explicitly unmaintained. Useful for lineage, not a sensible new product foundation.
